newsitem.title: UK: Clydeport Plc chief executive new to ports.
newsitem.headline: Clydeport Plc chief executive new to ports.

text.p: Clydeport Plc, the Glasgow-based port and property services group, has appointed a new chief executive with no ports experience in the wake of losing both its managing director and executive chairman over the past six months.
Clydeport said on Thursday it had appointed Tom Allison, 49, as chief executive. He will join the firm in September.
Allison is currently a director of CSC Forest Products, a Sterling-based joint venture between Glunz AG and Hann with annual turnover of around 250 million sterling and 1,300 employees.

He will face the immediate task of reviving investor interest in the company, which has seen its share price fall steadily this year from a high of 165 pence down to 119.5p at the London close on Thursday.

Allison said he intended to bed himself into his new position slowly since he has no direct experience of the ports industry. He has previously held senior management positions with Rank Xerox, ADT and Thistle Hotels.
He said: "My main objectives are quite simple: to work to maximize the commercial opportunities to the benefit of the customers, shareholders and staff."
Clydeport saw the unexpected resignations of managing director David Hunt in February and executive chairman John Mather in May.
Non-executive director James Millar stepped up to become non-executive chairman on Mr Mather's resignation, but finding a new chief executive has taken longer.
Millar denied Clydeport had been under pressure from institutional investors to find a new chief executive.

He said: "We haven't felt under great pressure since we have had such a great performance from the team that has stood in." Clydeport's three executive directors have shared day-to-day responsibility for running the company over the past six months, he said.
"As for heading off any concerns over the company, the best way to do that will be through the results," Millar added.
Clydeport is due to post interim results in the last week of August. - Julian Bray Reuters Shipping Desk +44 171 542 4087 Fax 5017
